- r marker: rows 51-53, columns 9-11 — a plus shape at (51-53, 9-11), center (52,10).
So Level 1: two floating bars (top N bar with r at (10,31); left Y bar with r at (34,10)), two containers (N container at rows 18-24; Y container at rows 35-47), and an r plus marker at (51-53, 9-11).
Clicks: (21,39) → rows 9-11 changed (N bar moved). (21,39) is inside the N container (rows 18-24, columns 36-48)! So clicking the N container moved the N bar. (38,24) → rows 31,33,34,35 changed (Y bar moved). (38,24) is inside the Y container (rows 35-47, columns 21-27)! So clicking the Y container moved the Y bar. (21,45) → rows 9-11 (N bar). (44,24) → Y bar.
So the rule is: click a container → the corresponding floating bar moves 3 rows/columns toward the container.
N bar: rows 9-11, columns 27-32, r at (10,31). N container: rows 18-24, columns 36-48. Clicking the container, the bar moved... rows 9-11 changed each time — the bar moved horizontally (columns) toward the container (rightward). The bar's r is at (10,31) on the right side — the bar moves in the direction of its r marker!
Y bar: rows 27-34, columns 9-11, r at (34,10) at the bottom. Y container is below (rows 35-47). The bar moved downward (3 rows per click) — in the direction of its r marker.
And the r plus at (51-53,9-11) is... probably a "goal" marker or decoration. Or maybe it indicates where the Y bar ultimately ends up? The Y bar ended at rows 46-50 (after 7 clicks from rows 28-32... wait, the Y bar started at rows 27-34 and ended at rows 46-50? After the step 26 click: rows 46-50. Container 2 is at rows 35-47. Hmm, the bar passed through the container? The bar at rows 46-50, columns 9-11 — but the container is at columns 21-27. The bar is at columns 9-11, not inside the container.
Wait, I might have misread. Let me recheck: the Y bar is at columns 9-11. Container 2 is at columns 21-27. The bar moved down at columns 9-11 and never entered the container. And the r plus is at (51-53, 9-11) — exactly where the bar ends up (rows 46-50 → next click → 49-53 → overlaps the plus!). So the goal is: move the bar onto the r plus marker!
So Level 1: click the container to move the bar 3 cells in the direction of its r end, until the bar reaches the r plus marker.
Hmm wait, but then what's the point of the container? Maybe the container is a "button" that moves the bar. The bar moves in the direction of its r marker. Goal: align the bar with the r plus.
Now Level 2:
- π shape (purple): top bar rows 9-11, columns 33-56; left leg rows 12-26, columns 33-35; right leg rows 15-44, columns 42-44.
- r plus at (30-32, 51-53), center (31,52).
- Piece at rows 36-41, columns 9-17, r at (37,16).
- Four containers at the bottom.
Mapping: in Level 1, the floating bars had r at one end. In Level 2, the piece has r at (37,16) (right side, middle row). The r plus is at (31,52).
But which object moves? In Level 1, the container was clicked and the bar moved. In Level 2, the containers are at the bottom (rows 54-60). Clicking them didn't move anything.
Hmm, maybe in Level 2 the π is the "container" (button), and clicking it moves the piece? The piece's r is at (37,16) on the right side → the piece moves right toward the r plus at (31,52)?
Or, the π itself is the movable object (like the bar), and the r plus is its target. The π's "r end" is... the π has no r.
Let me try: click the π (e.g., the top bar at (10,45), or the leg at (20,34)). If the π moves (toward the r plus?), that's the mechanic.
Actually, wait — maybe in Level 2, clicking a container moves the piece in the direction of the piece's r (right). I clicked the O container (56,6) — the piece didn't move. Hmm.
Maybe the piece only moves when the clicked container matches the color of the piece's r? No, r is r.
Let me try clicking the π. First try the top bar (10,45).
